questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_1
questions.text: Which one of the following best describes what the passage is trying to do?
options: It questions an explanation about how maps are designed.
It corrects the misconception about the way maps are designed.
It critiques a methodology used to create maps.
It explores some myths about maps.
questions.explanation: The author implicitly means that people have a preemptive notion of maps facing the north. He discusses why different people started putting north at the top. He mentions that the reasons for different people putting north at the top were different from what people think now and cites various examples to show that north's presence at the top is more recent and due to varied factors. Hence, he is trying to clear certain misconceptions about why north is put at the top in the maps.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_2
questions.text: Early maps did NOT put north at the top for all the following reasons EXCEPT
options: North was the source of darkness.
South was favoured by some emperors.
East and south were more important for religious reasons for some civilisations.
East was considered by some civilisations to be a more positive direction.
questions.explanation: The passage mentions that the Chinese put North at the top of the map because the emperor would live in the North and he preferred to look towards South. Hence, the fact that South was preferred by some emperors is not a reason why North was put at the top.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_3
questions.text: According to the passage, early Chinese maps placed north at the top because
options: the Chinese invented the compass and were aware of magnetic north.
they wanted to show respect to the emperor.
the Chinese emperor appreciated the winds from the south.
north was considered the most desirable direction.
questions.explanation: The passage states that the emperor lived in the north and hence maps depicted him as above his subjects. Thus, north was placed at the top of the map to show respect for the emperor.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_4
questions.text: It can be inferred from the passage that European explorers like Columbus and Megellan
options: set the precedent for north-up maps
navigated by the compass
used an eastward orientation for religious reasons
navigated with the help of early maps
questions.explanation: In the passage, it is given that "When Columbus describes the world it is in accordance with east being at the top, he says. 'Columbus says he is going towards paradise, so his mentality is from a medieval mappa mundi.'"

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_5
questions.text: Which one of the following about the northern orientation of modern maps is asserted in the passage?
options: The biggest contributory factor was the understanding of magnetic north.
The biggest contributory factor was the role of European explorers.
The biggest contributory factor was the influence of Christian maps.
The biggest contributory factor is not stated in the passage.
questions.explanation: The author explicitly refutes the role of the compass and of European explorers in placing North at the top of maps. While the author counters all known explanations as to why North was placed on the top, he does not offer any explanation of his own.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_6
questions.text: The role of natural phenomena in influencing map-making conventions is seen most clearly in
options: early Egyptian maps
early Islamic maps
early Chinese maps
early Christian maps
questions.explanation: According to the passage, early Egyptian maps placed the East at the top because that was the position of sunrise. Hence, natural phenomena dictated the map-making convention in this case.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_7
questions.text: The printing press has been likened to the Internet for which one of the following reasons?
options: It enabled rapid access to new information and the sharing of new ideas.
It represented new and revolutionary technology compared to the past.
It encouraged reading among people by giving them access to thousands of books.
It gave people access to pamphlets and literature in several languages.
questions.explanation: In the passage, the author mentions the printing press as the internet of its day. He further elucidates how the printing press helped in spreading ideas and information. Thus, the author likened the printing press to the internet because it enabled access to new information and sharing of ideas.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_8

gave people direct access to authentic medical information and religious texts.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_9
questions.text: Steve Jobs predicted which one of the following with the introduction of the iPhone?
options: People would switch from reading on the Internet to reading on their iPhones.
People would lose interest in historical and traditional classics.
Reading printed books would become a thing of the past.
The production of e-books would eventually fall.
questions.explanation: The author quotes Steve Jobs: "Not long after Steve Jobs introduced his iPhone, he said the bound book was probably headed for history's attic." Thus, we can infer that Steve Jobs predicted that reading printed books would become a thing of the past.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_varc_10
questions.text: "I'm still waiting to see if the iPhone can do what the printing press did for religion and democracy." The author uses which one of the following to indicate his uncertainty?
options: The rise of religious groups in many parts of the world.
The expansion in trolling and narcissism among users of the Internet.
The continued suppression of free speech in closed societies.
The decline in reading habits among those who use the device.

However, the failure of the Arab Spring and the continued suppression in places like North Korea shows that this has not happened. Hence, the author uses the continued suppression of free speech in closed societies to indicate why he is still uncertain about the potential of the iPhone.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_dilr_35
questions.text: Assume that only one client's order can be processed at any given point of time. So, Anish or Bani cannot start preparing a new order while a previous order is being prepared. At what time is the order placed by Client 1 completely served?
questions.explanation: Client 1 ordered 1 burger (10 min), 3 portions of fries (5 min machine time, no operator), and 1 ice cream (2 min). The burger takes 10 minutes to finish, and the other items can be completed within those 10 minutes. Thus, the order is complete at 10:10.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_dilr_36
questions.text: Assume that only one client's order can be processed at any given point of time. So, Anish or Bani cannot start preparing a new order while a previous order is being prepared. At what time is the order placed by Client 3 completely served?
questions.explanation: First order done at 10:10. Second order (two fries, one ice cream) done at 10:15. Third order is 1 burger and 1 portion of fries. Burger takes 10 minutes, fries are ready within that time. 10:15 + 10 mins = 10:25.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_dilr_37
questions.text: Suppose the employees are allowed to process multiple orders at a time, but the preference would be to finish orders of clients who placed their orders earlier. At what time is the order placed by Client 2 completely served?
questions.explanation: Anish and Bani work in parallel. For Client 1, burger done at 10:10, ice cream at 10:02, fries at 10:05. For Client 2 (at 10:05, ice cream and fries), Bani works on ice cream from 10:05 (finished 10:07) and puts fries (finished 10:10). The order is completed by 10:10.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_dilr_38
questions.text: Suppose the employees are allowed to process multiple orders at a time, but the preference would be to finish orders of clients who placed their orders earlier. Also assume that the fourth client came in only at 10:35. Between 10:00 and 10:30, for how many minutes is exactly one of the employees idle?
questions.explanation: After Client 1's burger is finished at 10:10 and Client 2's order is done, and Client 3's burger is started and finished at 10:17, one person (Anish) is free from 10:10 to 10:17 (7 minutes) plus the initial time Bani was free (10:02-10:05 = 3 minutes). Total idle time = 7+3 = 10 minutes.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_67
questions.text: Arun's present age in years is 40% of Barun's. In another few years, Arun's age will be half of Barun's. By what percentage will Barun's age increase during this period?
questions.explanation: Let Arun's current age be A. Hence, Barun's current age is 2.5A. Let Arun's age be half of Barun's age after X years. Therefore, 2*(X+A) = 2.5A + X. Or, X = 0.5A. Hence, Barun's age increased by 0.5A/2.5A = 20%.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_68
questions.text: A person can complete a job in 120 days. He works alone on Day 1. On Day 2, he is joined by another person who also can complete the job in exactly 120 days. On Day 3, they are joined by another person of equal efficiency. Like this, everyday a new person with the same efficiency joins the work. How many days are required to complete the job?
questions.explanation: Let the rate of work of a person be x units/day. Hence, the total work = 120x. It is given that on first day, one person works, on the second day two people work and so on. Hence, the work done on day 1, day 2,... will be x, 2x, 3x, ... respectively. The sum should be equal to 120x: 120x = x * [n(n+1)/2]. n^2 + n - 240 = 0. n = 15 is the only positive solution. Hence, it takes 15 days to complete the work.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_69
questions.text: An elevator has a weight limit of 630 kg. It is carrying a group of people of whom the heaviest weighs 57 kg and the lightest weighs 53 kg. What is the maximum possible number of people in the group?
questions.explanation: It is given that the maximum weight limit is 630. The lightest person's weight is 53 Kg and the heaviest person's weight is 57 Kg. In order to have maximum people in the lift, all the remaining people should be of the lightest weight possible, which is 53 Kg. Let there be n people: 53 + n(53) + 57 = 630. n is approximately 9.8. Hence, 9 additional people are possible. Therefore, a total of 9 + 2 = 11 people can use the elevator.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_70
questions.text: A man leaves his home and walks at a speed of 12 km per hour, reaching the railway station 10 minutes after the train had departed. If instead he had walked at a speed of 15 km per hour, he would have reached the station 10 minutes before the train's departure. The distance (in km) from his home to the railway station is
questions.explanation: He saves 20 minutes by changing speed from 12 km/hr to 15 km/hr. Let d be the distance. (d/12) - (d/15) = 20/60 = 1/3. (d/60) = 1/3. d = 20 km.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_71
questions.text: Ravi invests 50% of his monthly savings in fixed deposits. Thirty percent of the rest of his savings is invested in stocks and the rest goes into Ravi's savings bank account. If the total amount deposited by him in the bank (for savings account and fixed deposits) is Rs 59500, then Ravi's total monthly savings (in Rs) is
questions.explanation: Let his total savings be 100x. He invests 50x in fixed deposits. 30% of the rest (50x) is 15x, which is invested in stocks, and 35x goes to savings bank. Total in bank = 50x + 35x = 85x = 59500. x = 700. Hence, 100x = 70000.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_72
questions.text: If a seller gives a discount of 15% on retail price, she still makes a profit of 2%. Which of the following ensures that she makes a profit of 20%?
options: Give a discount of 5% on retail price.
Give a discount of 2% on retail price.
Increase the retail price by 2%.
Sell at retail price.
questions.explanation: Let retail price = M, cost price = C. 0.85M = 1.02C => M = (1.02/0.85)C = 1.2C. To make 20% profit, she must sell at 1.2C, which is exactly M (the retail price).

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_73
questions.text: A man travels by a motor boat down a river to his office and back. With the speed of the river unchanged, if he doubles the speed of his motor boat, then his total travel time gets reduced by 75%. The ratio of the original speed of the motor boat to the speed of the river is
questions.explanation: Let river speed = x, boat speed = u, distance = d. Initial time t = d/(u-x) + d/(u+x) = 2ud/(u^2 - x^2). Final time t/4 = d/(2u-x) + d/(2u+x) = 4ud/(4u^2 - x^2). Equating 2t/4 = t/2 = 4ud/(4u^2 - x^2) = ud/(u^2 - x^2). 8(u^2 - x^2) = 4u^2 - x^2. 4u^2 = 7x^2. u/x = √7/2.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_75
questions.text: The number of girls appearing for an admission test is twice the number of boys. If 30% of the girls and 45% of the boys get admission, the percentage of candidates who do not get admission is
questions.explanation: Let boys = 100, girls = 200. Admission: girls = 30% of 200 = 60, boys = 45% of 100 = 45. Total admitted = 105. Total candidates = 300. Not admitted = 300 - 105 = 195. Percentage = (195/300) * 100 = 65%.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_76
questions.text: A stall sells popcorn and chips in packets of three sizes: large, super, and jumbo. The numbers of large, super, and jumbo packets in its stock are in the ratio 7 : 17 : 16 for popcorn and 6 : 15 : 14 for chips. If the total number of popcorn packets in its stock is the same as that of chips packets, then the numbers of jumbo popcorn packets and jumbo chips packets are in the ratio
questions.explanation: Popcorn: 7x, 17x, 16x (Total 40x). Chips: 6y, 15y, 14y (Total 35y). Given 40x = 35y => 8x = 7y. Jumbo popcorn/Jumbo chips = 16x / 14y = (16x/14) * (8x/7x) = 16/14 * 8/7 = 1/1.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_77
questions.text: In a market, the price of medium quality mangoes is half that of good mangoes. A shopkeeper buys 80 kg good mangoes and 40 kg medium quality mangoes from the market and then sells all these at a common price which is 10% less than the price at which he bought the good ones. His overall profit is
questions.explanation: Price good = 2p, price medium = p. Cost = 80(2p) + 40(p) = 200p. Selling price = 0.9(2p) = 1.8p per kg. Total Revenue = 120 * 1.8p = 216p. Profit = 16p. Profit % = (16/200)*100 = 8%.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_78
questions.text: If Fatima sells 60 identical toys at a 40% discount on the printed price, then she makes 20% profit. Ten of these toys are destroyed in fire. While selling the rest, how much discount should be given on the printed price so that she can make the same amount of profit?
questions.explanation: Let printed price = M, Cost price = C. Selling price = 0.6M. Profit = 20% of Cost. 60(0.6M) = 60(1.2C) => 36M = 72C => M = 2C. Total Profit = 60(0.6M - C) = 60(1.2C - C) = 12C. Remaining toys = 50. Let new discount = d. SP = M(1-d). Total Revenue needed = Total Cost + Profit = 60C + 12C = 72C. 50 * M(1-d) = 72C. Substitute M=2C: 100C(1-d) = 72C => 1-d = 0.72 => d = 0.28 = 28%.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_80
questions.text: A class consists of 20 boys and 30 girls. In the mid-semester examination, the average score of the girls was 5 higher than that of the boys. In the final exam, however, the average score of the girls dropped by 3 while the average score of the entire class increased by 2. The increase in the average score of the boys is
questions.explanation: Let boy average = A. Girl average = A+5. Total score = 20A + 30(A+5) = 50A + 150. Average = A + 3. Final class average = A + 3 + 2 = A + 5. Total = 50(A+5) = 50A + 250. Girls final score = 30(A+5-3) = 30(A+2) = 30A + 60. Boys final score = (50A + 250) - (30A + 60) = 20A + 190. Boy final average = (20A+190)/20 = A + 9.5. Increase = A + 9.5 - A = 9.5.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_81
questions.text: The area of the closed region bounded by the equation |x| + |y| = 2 in the two-dimensional plane is
options: 4π sq. units
4 sq. units
8 sq. units
2π sq. units
questions.explanation: The equation |x| + |y| = 2 forms a square with vertices at (2,0), (0,2), (-2,0), (0,-2). The length of each side is √[2^2 + 2^2] = √8. Area = side^2 = 8.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_82
questions.text: From a triangle ABC with sides of lengths 40 ft, 25 ft and 35 ft, a triangular portion GBC is cut off where G is the centroid of ABC. The area, in sq ft, of the remaining portion of triangle ABC is
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 100, s = 50. Area = √[50(10)(25)(15)] = √187500 = 250√3. The area of the triangle GBC formed by the centroid is 1/3 the area of the original triangle. Remaining area = 2/3 of 250√3 = 500√3/3.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_83
questions.text: Let ABC be a right-angled isosceles triangle with hypotenuse BC. Let BQC be a semi-circle, away from A, with diameter BC. Let BPC be an arc of a circle centered at A and lying between BC and BQC. If AB has length 6 cm then the area, in sq cm, of the region enclosed by BPC and BQC is
options: 9π
questions.explanation: AB=AC=6, BC=6√2. Radius of semi-circle = 3√2. Area = 1/2 * π * (3√2)^2 = 9π. Area of sector BPC (angle 90°) = 1/4 * π * 6^2 = 9π. Area of region = Area(semi-circle) - [Area(sector) - Area(ABC)] = 9π - [9π - 18] = 18.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_84
questions.text: A solid metallic cube is melted to form five solid cubes whose volumes are in the ratio 1 : 1 : 8 : 27 : 27. The percentage by which the sum of the surface areas of these five cubes exceeds the surface area of the original cube is nearest to
questions.explanation: Let volumes be x, x, 8x, 27x, 27x. Total = 64x. Side of original cube A = 4a. Surface area = 6*(4a)^2 = 96a^2. Sides of new cubes: a, a, 2a, 3a, 3a. Areas: 6a^2, 6a^2, 24a^2, 54a^2, 54a^2. Sum = 144a^2. Increase % = (144-96)/96 = 48/96 = 50%.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_85
questions.text: A ball of diameter 4 cm is kept on top of a hollow cylinder standing vertically. The height of the cylinder is 3 cm, while its volume is 9π cubic centimeters. Then the vertical distance, in cm, of the topmost point of the ball from the base of the cylinder is
questions.explanation: Volume of cylinder = π * r^2 * h = 9π. With h=3, r^2=3, r=√3. Ball radius R=2. Since R > r, the ball sits on the rim of the cylinder. Using Pythagoras in the triangle formed by cylinder axis, radius r, and ball radius R, the ball center sits at height h + √[R^2 - r^2] = 3 + √[4-3] = 4. Topmost point = 4 + 2 = 6 cm.

questions.id: CAT 2017 Slot 1 Question Paper by Cracku_qa_86
questions.text: Let ABC be a right-angled triangle with BC as the hypotenuse. Lengths of AB and AC are 15 km and 20 km, respectively. The minimum possible time, in minutes, required to reach the hypotenuse from A at a speed of 30 km per hour is
questions.explanation: Sides 15:20:25. Shortest distance = altitude = (15*20)/25 = 12 km. Time = 12 km / 30 kmph = 0.4 hours = 24 minutes.

questions.text: Let AB, CD, EF, GH, and JK be five diameters of a circle with center at 0. In how many ways can three points be chosen out of A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, J, K, and O so as to form a triangle?
questions.explanation: Total points = 11. Combinations = 11C3 = 165. Subtract collinear cases: 5 diameters each contain 3 points (2 ends + center). 5 * 3C3 = 5 triangles not possible. 165 - 5 = 160.

questions.explanation: y = |x-1| + |x+1|. If -1 ≤ x ≤ 1, y = 2. If x > 1, y = 2x. If x < -1, y = -2x. The curve is a line y=2 between x=-1 and x=1. The distance from (0.5, 1) to the line y=2 is |2-1| = 1.

questions.text: Let a1, a2,..., a3n be an arithmetic progression with a1 = 3 and a2 = 7. If a1 + a2 +...+ a3n = 1830, then what is the smallest positive integer m such that m(a1 + a2 +...+ an) > 1830?
